title: Pawn chains: attack the base

D0.outcome: Explains a pawn chain with its base and head and why play splits into two fronts: the cramped wing and the base.

D1.outcome: In a French-advance type structure, names the lever that attacks the base and the plan for the chain's owner on the other wing.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled chain positions, picks the plan for each side and tells an attack on the base from an attack on the head.

D3.outcome: Chooses between a siege and a war of movement, transfers the attack to a second weakness, and predicts how timing (too early) or piece placement changes the answer.

misconceptions: Attack the head of the chain.
Freeing operations against a chain cannot start too early.
conditions: A real chain with a fixed head and base.
Every chain owner also has a base of his own to protect.
contrasts: Hitting the head of the chain (the ...f6 lever) instead of the base.
Starting the liberating operation too early; 'cannot begin too early' is too absolute.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.OUTPOST.D2: the square in front of the chain's head is often an outpost
